questions.question: 77.5% of this IPO's money is an offer for sale. Where does that part of the money go?

choices.text: Into the company, to build new factories.
To the existing owners who are selling their shares.

questions.explanation: In an offer for sale, existing owners sell shares they already hold, so the money goes to them. Only the fresh issue, ₹150 crore here, reaches SFC Environmental Technologies Limited.

questions.question: Sales went from ₹657.50 crore in FY24 to ₹803.63 crore in FY26, which is 10.6% a year. How would you describe that?
questions.explanation: 10.6% a year is slow growth: SFC Environmental Technologies Limited is growing, but not by much.

questions.question: SFC Environmental Technologies Limited owes 0.24 rupees of loans for every rupee of its owners' money. Which is closest to the truth?

choices.text: Its loans are small to manageable next to what the owners have put in.
Its loans are heavy: lenders have more riding on it than its owners.
Loans never matter for a company that makes a profit.

questions.explanation: At 0.24 rupees of loans per rupee of owners' money, SFC Environmental Technologies Limited's owners have more in the business than its lenders.

questions.question: An unofficial grey market premium of ₹21 a share is being quoted. How much should you rely on it?

choices.text: Completely: it tells you the listing price.
A little at most: it is unregulated and easy to push around.
It is set by the stock exchange.

questions.explanation: The grey market premium of ₹21 for SFC Environmental Technologies Limited is gossip with a number on it: nobody regulates it, and it often turns out wrong.
